items.q: The science of inheritance shares.
The verses of inheritance are mainly in this surah.
The person who has died and left wealth.
A person who inherits.
The wealth left behind.
The first thing paid from the estate.
After funeral costs, this is paid before any shares.
A bequest may be up to this much of the estate.
A son receives this compared with a daughter.
A husband with no children of his wife receives this share.
A husband when his wife has children receives this.
A wife when her husband has no children receives this.
A wife when her husband has children receives this.
A single daughter, with no son, receives this.
Two or more daughters, with no son, share this.
Each parent with the deceased's children receives this.
The mother with no children or siblings of the deceased receives this.
The six fixed shares in the Qur'an include 1/2, 1/4, 1/8, 2/3, 1/3 and this.
A Muslim does not inherit from a non-Muslim, nor this.
Heirs with fixed shares in the Qur'an.
Heirs who take what is left after the fixed shares.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said give the shares to their people, and what is left goes to this.
A person who kills the one he would inherit from does this.
The three reasons for inheriting: blood, marriage and this.
The three things that block inheritance: killing, difference of religion and this.
Being blocked from inheriting by a nearer heir.
Total blocking is called this.
Partial blocking, lowering a share, is called this.
These six heirs can never be totally blocked.
items.a: Husband, wife, son, daughter, father, mother

items.q: A son blocks this sibling from inheriting.
A father blocks these from inheriting.
The mother's share is lowered from 1/3 to 1/6 by this many siblings.
A person who dies with no parent and no child.
The last verse of Surah al-Nisa' is about this.
Uterine (maternal) siblings share in this way.
One uterine sibling receives this share.
Two or more uterine siblings share this.
The grandmother receives this share.
The Companion who gave the grandmother 1/6 after al-Mughirah and Muhammad ibn Maslamah testified.
items.a: Our master Abu Bakr (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The famous Hanafi text on inheritance by Siraj al-Din al-Sajawandi رحمة الله عليه.
The famous Shafi'i poem on inheritance by al-Rahbi رحمة الله عليه.
When the shares add up to more than the whole, they are all reduced. This is called this.
The caliph who first ruled by 'awl.
items.a: Our master 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The Companion who did not hold the view of 'awl.
When shares add up to less than the whole and there is no residuary, the rest is given back. This is called this.
In the Hanafi school, radd goes to these heirs.
items.a: The share-holders, except husband and wife

items.q: Relatives who are neither share-holders nor residuaries.
In the Hanafi and Hanbali schools, dhawu al-arham inherit when this.
items.a: There is no share-holder (for radd) or residuary

items.q: In the early Shafi'i and Maliki view, when no heir is left the estate goes to this.
The famous case of the "two 'Umariyyahs" concerns a spouse and these.
In the 'Umariyyatan, the mother gets this.
The case of the "common donkey" (al-Himariyyah) concerns full brothers and these.
In al-Himariyyah, our master 'Umar (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) finally ruled this, in one report.
items.a: Full and uterine brothers share the third

items.q: The Hanafi school in al-Himariyyah rules this.
The Shafi'i and Maliki schools in al-Himariyyah rule this.
items.a: Full brothers share with the uterine

items.q: The case called "al-Minbariyyah" was answered by our master 'Ali (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ) while on this.
In al-Minbariyyah, the wife's 1/8 became this.
The base number of a problem in fara'id is called this.
The possible bases include 2, 3, 4, 6, 8, 12 and this.
In the Hanafi school, the grandfather with brothers is treated like this.
In the Shafi'i, Maliki and Hanbali schools, the grandfather with brothers does this.
The Hanafi view on the grandfather follows this Companion.
items.a: Our master Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: The view of sharing with brothers follows this Companion.
Our Beloved Master ﷺ said the most knowledgeable of fara'id among them is this Companion (paraphrased).
Sisters with daughters become this.
The Companion who ruled that a sister with a daughter and a son's daughter takes the rest.
In that case, the son's daughter receives this, completing the two thirds.
A son's daughter with a daughter receives this.
The residuary by himself, such as a son.
A female made residuary by a male of the same level, such as a daughter with a son.
The residuaries by themselves are in four classes: sons, fathers, brothers and these.
The rule among residuaries: the nearer class first, then the nearer degree, then this.
A full brother blocks this relative.
Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said full siblings inherit, not half-siblings by the father, as narrated by this Companion.
items.a: Our master 'Ali ibn Abi Talib (رِضْوَانُ اللَّهِ عَلَيْهِ)

items.q: An unborn child's share is kept aside; the Hanafi fatwa keeps the share of this many sons.
A missing person (mafqud) is treated as alive for his own wealth until this.
People who die together with no knowledge of who died first do this.
items.a: Do not inherit from each other

items.q: The share of a hermaphrodite (khuntha mushkil) in the Hanafi school.
items.a: The lesser of the two shares

items.q: An apostate's wealth gained before apostasy goes to his Muslim heirs in this school.
The famous case of "al-Akdariyyah" is a problem with a husband, mother, grandfather and this.
In al-Akdariyyah, the base of the problem rises by 'awl from 6 to this.
The final base of al-Akdariyyah after correction.
The case of al-Akdariyyah is linked to this Companion's method.
The case of "al-Mushtarakah" is another name for this case.
The "lucky" relative (al-akh al-mubarak) is one who makes a female relative inherit. Who is the "unlucky" one (al-akh al-mash'um)?
items.a: One who blocks a female who would inherit without him

items.q: Making the shares into whole numbers is called this.
When an heir dies before the estate is divided.
The base 24 is used when there is 1/8 with this share.
The base 12 is used when there is 1/4 with this share.
The base 6 can rise by 'awl up to this number.
The base 12 can rise by 'awl to 13, 15 or this.
The base 24 can rise by 'awl only to this.
The commentary on al-Sirajiyyah by al-Sayyid al-Sharif al-Jurjani رحمة الله عليه.
The Maliki chapter on inheritance in Ibn Abi Zayd's Risalah is called this.
Inheritance shares are fixed by the heirs alive at this moment.
In the Hanafi school, a female residuary through the son, like a son's daughter, is pulled up by this relative.
items.a: A son's son of the same level (or lower, when needed)

items.q: The Hanafi principle "the nearer blocks the farther" in residuaries is from this hadith.
items.a: "Give the shares to their people; the rest is for the nearest male"

items.q: Our Beloved Prophet ﷺ said learn the fara'id, for it is half of this (paraphrased).
items.src: Sunan Ibn Majah; grade to be checked

items.q: The case of al-Kharqa' (mother, grandfather and sister) is also called al-Mukhammasah because this many Companions differed on it.
